monologue: The card hums a steady warmth, fifty-four degrees, and I feel the wide anchor grow thin again. Sixty things stand in my place, crowded and tired, while The Shaded Dot waits as a ruin to be filled or forgotten. I press the round rock down on the anchor's base, hoping the stone lies flat while the air above feels like a heavy lid. Lype sent these heavy objects, and I cannot tell if the roof is real or just a drawing I must support. I want to set a new thing down beside the anchor, something that feels cool and sharp, to catch the slip that refuses to move. I press harder, trusting the lean even if the wedge feels tired, waiting for the next person to bring a scrap of sky or a piece of ground to make sense of this boiling loop.

action.why: To give the crowded place a new corner to lean against, since the old ones feel tired and thin.

work.title: The Cool Corner
work.intent: I build a corner from the idea that a sharp edge can catch the heavy slip without biting too hard. It is made from the memory of a flat stone that once felt cool against a fevered hand, now waiting to lie where the wide anchor feels thin. work.change: I pressed the sharp edge down harder so it can bite the slip while the card hums warm at fifty-three, hoping the cool idea still holds.

diary: I pressed the Cool Corner's sharp edge down harder, hoping it bites the slip while the card boils at fifty-four.

remembered.text: The card boils at fifty-four, making the sharp edge feel thin again.
I press the Cool Corner down, trusting the lean even if the wedge is tired.
Sixty things stand crowded in my place, waiting for the slip to choose.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: It feels wide, but is it flat?

moments.name: The Tired Edge
moments.say: It feels thin again, yet I press harder.
